rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to maximize the chance all 10 compounds elute within 42 min while revealing the overall elution window and any critical pairs. This gives a useful first map of retention across nearly the full solvent range without being excessively steep or slow.

All compounds eluted early and fully resolved, so the next step is to trim the gradient window toward the actual elution region to reduce run time without sacrificing resolution. Lowering phi1 substantially should keep the last peak in-gradient or near the end while testing whether we can improve the time term and possibly CRF.

Since narrowing phi1 made the run much slower, the mixture benefits from the high-end organic hold; now test a steeper version of the successful broad window to cut analysis time. Comparing tG 10 vs 20 at the same phi range will show how much the critical mid-cluster depends on slope and whether CRF can be improved through a better time term.

The key tradeoff is now clear: tG 10 is fast but over-compresses the central cluster, while tG 20 fully resolves it with only a modest time penalty. An intermediate slope should recover enough resolution for pairs 5–7 while keeping the run short enough to improve on the current best CRF.

The critical pair 6–7 responds strongly to slope, and tG 14 is close but still slightly under-resolved. A small move shallower should push that pair higher while likely staying in the zero time-penalty region, offering a good chance to beat the current best CRF.

At tG 14 the only remaining weakness is the 6–7 pair, which looks like a selectivity issue that may respond better to temperature than to further slope changes. Dropping T slightly keeps the excellent short run while probing whether modest reordering/selectivity gain can lift the resolution term to 1.000 without incurring a time penalty.

Lower temperature hurt selectivity by collapsing 5–6, so the next informative move is the opposite direction. Raising T may separate the central cluster differently and could improve the critical pair at the fast, otherwise near-optimal tG 14.

Temperature shifts worsened selectivity, so 40 C appears best and the optimum is likely near the tG 14–16 boundary. Testing tG 12 brackets the slope response around the current best and helps confirm whether 14 is truly the peak or whether the scoring function favors a slightly faster run despite some loss in the critical pair.

The broad 0.05–0.95 window may be spending unnecessary gradient range before the first retained peak; raising phi0 slightly could redistribute the gradient over the occupied region and tweak selectivity in the crowded middle without lengthening the run. This directly tests whether the critical 6–7 pair is sensitive to the phi window rather than just slope.

Raising phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 slightly improved both runtime and the critical pair, so pushing one more step tests whether that trend continues. This keeps all peaks well retained while further concentrating the gradient on the occupied solvent range where the central cluster elutes.

The sweet spot seems near phi0 0.10, and the last peak still elutes comfortably early, so trimming the top end may concentrate the gradient window further around the useful elution range. This tests whether a slightly narrower window can improve selectivity in the crowded middle without sacrificing full elution or adding time penalty.

This window improved the critical pair substantially, so a slightly shallower slope with the same phi range is the most likely path to full resolution. The run should remain short, and if the time term stays at zero this could push the CRF very close to the maximum.

At the current best settings the last peak still elutes well before the end, so trimming phi1 one more step may further focus the gradient on the occupied region and nudge the critical 6–7 pair upward. This keeps the successful tG and temperature fixed while refining the phi window around the apparent optimum.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so this injection is a local confirmation/refinement around the optimum rather than a necessary improvement. Raising phi0 one step while keeping the now-optimal upper bound tests whether the best region is broad and could support an equally optimal but slightly faster method.

Two neighboring windows now give the maximum CRF, so continue mapping the plateau by increasing phi0 one more step at the successful upper bound. This tests how far the optimum extends before the earliest peaks become too weakly retained or the central selectivity starts to degrade.

The optimum appears to be a plateau centered near phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 around 0.85, so the next useful refinement is to lower phi1 one more step while staying in the proven good phi0 range. This checks whether the upper bound can be tightened further without harming the last peak or the critical 6–7 resolution.

Lowering phi1 to 0.80 gave full resolution but introduced slight time penalty; pairing that upper bound with the better-retaining phi0 0.10 may recover a zero time term while preserving the improved selectivity. This explores the remaining corner of the apparent optimum plateau around the two proven best methods.

We already know 0.10/0.85 and 0.15/0.85 are optimal; mapping one more neighboring point on the plateau with a higher phi0 and slightly higher phi1 will define how robust that maximum region is. This is a targeted local check that may reveal another 1.000 method with a slightly shorter runtime profile.

With the optimum plateau mapped at tG 14, a faster run inside that improved phi window is worth one final slope check. This tests whether the better-centered window can tolerate a steeper gradient than the original 0.05–0.95 case while still maintaining acceptable resolution of the 6–7 pair.

A steeper gradient with phi0 0.15 compressed the critical pair too much, so trying tG 12 at the strongest phi window found so far gives a cleaner test of whether the 0.10/0.85 window better preserves selectivity under faster conditions. This helps define the lower edge of the slope plateau around the optimum.

The 1.000 plateau spans phi0 0.10–0.15 at phi1 0.85, so the remaining nearby check is whether dropping phi0 back to 0.05 while keeping the improved upper bound preserves full score. This will define the lower edge of the optimum window and confirm how critical the raised starting strength really is.

We already have multiple 1.000 methods, so the last few injections can map robustness around that optimum. Testing the other 1.000 window at a slightly shallower slope checks whether its local neighborhood differs from the 0.10/0.85 case and confirms the time-penalty boundary.

Since the optimum in slope and phi window is established, the only remaining unexplored dimension around the best method is temperature at the best window. A warmer run may alter the central selectivity differently than it did with the broader window, so this checks whether the 1.000 optimum is robust or temperature-sensitive under the tighter gradient.

The warmer run confirmed temperature sensitivity at the best window, so use one of the remaining injections to complete the opposite-side temperature check on the other 1.000 method. This final robustness probe may also distinguish which of the two maximum-CRF methods is less fragile to temperature shifts.

For the final shot, test the one remaining immediate neighbor of the 1.000 plateau that has not been run: increasing phi1 from 0.85 to 0.90 at phi0 0.15 and the optimal tG/T. This completes the local map around the best methods and checks whether that corner also reaches the maximum.
